title: How To Use the Jasper × Jira Integration: Keep the Work on the Ticket That Tracks It
summary: The Jasper Jira integration sends finished content from Jasper into a Jira issue, so the deliverable sits on the ticket your team is already tracking it with. This guide covers what it does, why it matters, and how to turn it on.
body_markdown:
Marketing teams use Jira because it keeps requests, deliverables, and status in one clear queue. But the board tracks the work more often than it contains it. A ticket says “In Review,” while the actual draft lives in a doc, attachment, or thread someone has to find.


Atlassian's[State of Teams 2026 CMO Brief](https://www.atlassian.com/blog/guides-research/the-state-of-teams-2026-cmo-brief) found that 94% of marketers now use AI at work, while only 3% of CMOs are certain they see AI ROI across the organization. Atlassian calls the difference a fragmentation tax: speed gained inside a function, lost in the coordination around it. Content is the clearest case. A team can fill a backlog faster than it can move one, and a fuller queue helps nobody if the deliverable on each ticket lives somewhere the board cannot point to.


## What is the Jasper × Jira integration?


The integration sends content created in[Jasper Canvas](https://www.jasper.ai/canvas) and[Jasper Grid](https://www.jasper.ai/grid) into a Jira issue. Open the finished piece in Jasper, choose how it should reach the issue, select the issue, and export. The content arrives on the ticket with a link back to where it came from.


Jira keeps doing what it does well. The issue carries the assignee, the status, the sprint, the epic, and its place on the board. Jasper handles the content. Jira handles the queue. That works for one piece or a batch: generate a run of variants in Grid and route each one to the ticket it belongs to, instead of distributing files by hand afterward.


## Why does it matter?


A board is only as useful as what its tickets point at. When the deliverable is attached to the issue, the status stops being a claim about work nobody can see, and reviewing something takes zero excavation.


The quality of what lands there matters just as much. Content produced in Jasper runs through[Jasper IQ](https://www.jasper.ai/jasper-iq) , which brings your[brand voice](https://www.jasper.ai/brand-voice) , approved messaging, and[Company Knowledge](https://www.jasper.ai/knowledge-base) into the output itself. The draft on the ticket already sounds like your brand, so reviewers give it the check it actually needs rather than resetting voice first, and tickets clear their workflow states in fewer passes.


The link back to the live Jasper document does the rest. A ticket that points at its source stays accurate after export, so whoever opens it last is not guessing whether they have the current copy.


## How do you set it up?


A Jasper Admin or Developer switches Jira on for the workspace under Workspace Settings > Team Integrations. After that, every user connects individually: Workspace Settings > Integrations, toggle Jira on, authenticate with your Jira credentials.


Full steps live in the[Jasper Help Center](https://help.jasper.ai/hc/en-us/articles/52722575595803-Integrations-Jira) .


## How do you send content from Jasper to Jira?


Open the finished piece in Canvas or Grid, hit Export, and select Jira. Choose the issue, and the content lands on it. Check that Jira is toggled on in your integrations panel before your first export.


### Choose how the content reaches the issue


You control how the content shows up on the ticket. Three options:


1. **Link to the Jasper doc.** A comment on the issue points to the live document in Jasper, so reviewers open the current copy and their edits stay in the source. Best while the copy is still changing.
2. **Attach the file.** The content is attached directly to the issue, and a comment adds the Jasper doc link alongside it. Best when someone outside Jasper needs to open or forward the copy.
3. **Save to cloud storage.** The content goes to your connected storage, whether that is Google Drive, SharePoint, or Box, and the issue gets a comment linking to it plus a link back to the Jasper doc. Best when finished assets belong in a shared library.


Pick one and hold the team to it. Consistency here is what keeps a ticket and its content pointed at each other after the sprint closes.


## How marketing teams put this to work


If your team runs its work as tickets on a board, the integration fits a job you already do every cycle: get the deliverable to the person whose turn it is.


### Content teams working a backlog


An editorial calendar in Jira is a backlog of tickets moving through drafting, review, and published. Exporting each finished piece to its ticket means the draft, the reviewer, and the status all sit in one place, and a piece stuck at a stage is visible along with the reason.


### Product marketing planning against a release board


Launch content can attach to the epic the release is scoped under, so the announcement and enablement copy carry the same date as everything else in that epic. When the date moves, the content moves with it rather than being written twice.


### Regional and localization teams


A team producing market variants can generate the full set in Grid and export each one to its own ticket, so every locale has an owner, a status, and its copy in the same object. Reviewing 12 markets becomes reading 12 tickets instead of reconciling one spreadsheet against a folder.


## Looking ahead


Work management tools are built to track the state of work, and they do it well. Holding the work itself was never the job. For marketing, where the deliverable is the point, that leaves a board full of accurate statuses pointing at content that takes a search to find. Putting the content on the ticket closes the gap: marketing keeps working in Jasper, the board keeps running the queue.


As AI pushes volume up, the advantage goes to teams whose deliverables sit where the work is tracked, not two tools away from it.


## Frequently asked questions


**Can I export from Grid, or only from Canvas?**


Both. A single document and a full Grid run of variants follow the same path, with each piece routed to the ticket it belongs to.


‍ **What actually appears on the Jira issue?**


Depends on the option you pick at export: a comment linking to the live Jasper doc, the file attached to the issue with that link added as a comment, or a comment linking to the copy in your connected cloud storage (Google Drive, SharePoint, or Box) plus the Jasper doc link. Storage has to be connected before you can use the third option.


‍ **What does setup require from my team?**


**‍** Two steps by two different roles. A Jasper Admin or Developer turns Jira on for the workspace, then each user authenticates their own Jira account. No IT project required.


‍ **Will the issue still point to the current copy after I export?**


Yes. All three options add a link to the live Jasper document, so anyone opening the ticket later gets the current copy rather than a snapshot from export day.


‍ **How does this hold brand standards as our content volume grows?**


Brand consistency has to be built in where content is made, not enforced after it travels. Jasper IQ applies your brand voice, approved messaging, and Company Knowledge at generation, so the copy is aligned before it reaches Jira. That holds the same whether you export one announcement or a quarter's worth of assets.
